findings.evidence: referenceBatch sets batching=true; assertIdle rejects a nested referenceBatch or guardNode preflight. But the exported qualify/predecessorReference call side() and comparisonBytes calls comparisonCore() without checking batching. During batch's member(row.after), a supplied callback holding the already-created subject can call subject.qualify, predecessorReference, or comparisonBytes; that reenters member and can execute another supplied read while the original batch remains active.
findings.impact: The batching lock does not cover all public methods entering its shared read/physical scope. A same-instance callback can reenter the batch's protected operation and alter callback/observation sequence, contrary to the proposed same-instance guard-idle contract. This is a concrete possible callback path in the new public subject API, not a claim it currently occurs on a production factory route.
findings.recommendation: Reject entry to public side/comparison during batching before any member callback, e.g. a narrow batching-only idle check that leaves any existing non-batch independent-method behavior unchanged; batch itself may continue using its private cores. Add real subject callback tests for each public method, alternate graph and second batch, verify no nested supplied callback and finally recovery.
findings.resolution: Resolved in the subsequently inspected working-tree update on both roots: public side() and comparisonBytes() check batching===false before invoking private core/member; batch uses private cores. The check is deliberately batching-only, leaving prior non-batch public side operations during normal guard consume unchanged. ownsReference remains a pure no-read query. Whole guard/alternate plan and nested batch already check assertIdle; batching clears in finally.

table_mapping: Packet and SELF bootstrap remain original member calls. Only the actual authenticated packet's ordered code_transitions.after and source_members are submitted to referenceBatch on the actual repairs object. Each static reference still invokes qualify, and comparison only when the same actual repairs.ownsReference says it is owned. Results are positioned per occurrence; no path-based dedup. Unknown qualifier null falls back to original ref and unknown comparison is never invented.

Each staticMember checks ref vs positional snapshot before and after actual read, gets physical before, compares actual supplied Buffer to that physical, rereads physical after, validates original logical comparison SHA/size and qualified actual SHA, compares raw against readEvidenceMember, and binds actual bytes by ref. Literal prior Git-data proof, expected transformed contents, transition order, dynamic registry/ledger/roster/frames/side operations remain unchanged. Its grouped local resolution contains expected DATA/ref results, not a saved current-state verdict.

If referenceBatch is absent, optional staticResolutions yields undefined and member uses the original per-reference qualify/owns/comparison code. Present non-data batch method rejects closed. No same-path or cross-instance reuse is introduced. At constructor end its real assertCurrent rechecks actual lane, frames, repairs and local bound final; this remains necessary after all staticMember callbacks.
shared_helper_contract: Public side and comparison retain their existing single-operation behavior, including side null without original physical sweep and comparison errors. Batch snapshots plain request graph, checks exact request fields, kind and metadata, authenticates planner and physical bound before first member callback, executes one actual sideCore/comparisonCore per request (each qualifying known ref rereads row.after physical/supplied/physical), revalidates whole request list around callbacks, then full physical bound and planner again. It retains no batch success across calls.

Cold batch sweep adds checks for all-unknown requests where original independent side calls returned null before a sweep; this is limited to new explicit batch API and actual table route. The operation intentionally changes callback order: all resolution callbacks precede table member reads. Per-member actual physical/supplied/physical and final guard are therefore material safeguards, not proof of continuous immutability.

Snapshot uses original plain() data semantics and deep content equality; it checks data/enumerability but does not preserve original writable/configurable flags, as existing single side metadata snapshot also uses plain. If stronger descriptor-flag immutability is an explicit batch contract, tests and implementation must add it; do not claim it now.

The current referenceBatch accepts a nonempty arbitrary-size array and plain recursive structures. The requested use is a finite authenticated packet; if the exposed API needs a deliberate size/depth bound, define it explicitly rather than claiming a measured bound. Plain original semantics may throw on cyclic input; no new current byte cache is present.
